name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 partisan lean in a Chicago-area district
Incumbent Jonathan Jackson running for reelection
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The district's strong Democratic lean, an incumbent seeking reelection, and a large fundraising edge all point to a comfortable Jackson win, and markets agree. No polls or expert ratings contradict the fundamentals-based picture.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending against Jackson or unusually low turnout in Chicago could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to flip the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jonathan Jackson, the Democratic incumbent in this heavily Democratic Chicago-area district, is seeking another term against Republican Christian Maxwell. The seat's partisan lean of D+18 makes a Republican win extremely unlikely in any plausible environment. Jackson also holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $418,000 to Maxwell's about $63,000, with no outside spending reported on either side.

Prediction markets price Jackson's chances at roughly 95 percent, consistent with the fundamentals. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district lean, incumbency, and money. All available evidence points to a safe Democratic hold with a margin in the low-to-mid twenties.
